findings.claim: The same-day grace confirmation is gated on hasLiveGame (moveCount > 0), so a zero-move challenge attempt is reset with no dialog and day D can never earn its on-time award again.
findings.note: PREDICATE FIXED, COVERAGE INCOMPLETE. Verified: Game.swift:436 is `(moveCount > 0 || graceLive) && !won && !demoing && !boardComplete`; index.html:1860 is the twin. I enumerated every hasLiveGame reader on both platforms — iOS ContentView:291 (deal alert), ContentView:344 (requestReset), DailyView:313 (daily Play), DailyView:375 (demo pill); web confirmReset only, called from newBtn:1886, replayBtn:1920, goDeal:1850. All are confirm gates, none is a resume banner / autosave / stats path, so no unintended user-visible change (RegressionDiscardConfirmTests both PASS on udid 5329250C, so no collateral). Zero-move copy verified reachable-only-via-grace, so the dropped cost sentence cannot print 'your 0 moves'. RESIDUAL: the grace is still silently forfeited through the re-deal entry points that never consulted hasLiveGame — see ux/index.html:daily-play-and-wins-bypass-hasLiveGame. Also note the closeout mutant c-ios-hasLiveGame-bare-movecount is killed only by the SOURCE-TEXT pin at tests/ios-parity.test.mjs:573-575; there is no behavioural test of the iOS predicate (the web one at tests/web-behaviour.test.mjs:160 is genuinely executed).

findings.claim: Every new iOS guard is a `body.includes(...)` / occurrence-count string pin, which detects EDITS to the quoted lines but is structurally blind to an INSERTED line, so a spliced `if 1 == 1 { return false }` disables the iOS tier chips and both auto-play refusals with every pin green.
findings.note: FIXED FOR THE THREE NAMED FUNCTIONS: both of my round-1 survivors are now killed (x-ios-objViolated-early-false, x-ios-autoSend-early-false), and I re-ran the manifest myself — 9/9 killed, 0 survived, errors 0, so the kills are real applies. The kill is TEXTUAL, not behavioural (Swift is only ever read as a string here), which is acceptable only because there is no Swift unit-test target in the project — ios/Causeway has CausewayUITests only. RESIDUAL: the pin stops at the three function boundaries; collaborators reached from inside them are still substring-only. Tracked as tests/ios-parity.test.mjs:helpers-unpinned-insertions.

findings.claim: The look-ahead's projection depth was unconstrained: `moves:moveCount+1` -> `moves:moveCount` and `moveIdx:moveCount+1` -> a constant both survived the whole suite, so an off-by-one in the projection would ship as a live scoring bug on moves-family days.
findings.note: VERIFIED, and killed for the RIGHT reason: the new day-boundary tests drive the SHIPPED lifted autoSendWouldBreakTier and observe its true/false return; `grep -n 'moveCount+1' tests/*.mjs` shows no text pin on index.html:700-701, so nothing textual could be doing the killing. My own re-run: x-web-lookahead-depth-off, x-web-lookahead-moveidx-off and x-web-lookahead-moveidx-plus-two all KILLED (9/9, 0 errors), i.e. the guard is two-sided. I also independently checked the implementer's `moveCount+1` reasoning rather than accepting it: index.html:713 (and the tableau twin a few lines below) does `moveCount++; setMoves(moveCount); recordHomed();` and recordHomed stamps `moveIdx:moveCount` at index.html:474-475 AFTER the increment; the Swift twin does `moveCount += 1; recordHomed()` (Game.swift:701,710) with recordHomed stamping `moveIdx: moveCount` (Game.swift:457,462) and commit() at :469-470 the same. The projection is correct in both copies — no live scoring bug. I additionally mutated the PRE-check (index.html:696 `moves:moveCount` -> `moves:0`): KILLED by the new `already lost` assertion, so the test constrains both the base and the projection.

findings.claim: extractDecl matched an INDENTED (nested) declaration anywhere in index.html and took the first textual match, so a future local helper with a colliding name would silently swap the code under test.
findings.note: VERIFIED by experiment, not by reading: an indented decoy is now ignored in BOTH orders, a nested-only declaration throws, two flush-left declarations throw with line numbers. I also checked the anchor against the real file — for all 29 NAMES the count of column-0 matches equals the count of matches anywhere in index.html, so nothing currently declared is being missed by the stricter anchor, and no name is declared twice. Column-0 decoys inside a template literal or a /* */ block DO false-positive, but they throw (loud) rather than silently swapping the code under test, which is the safe direction. The `NAMES.map(n => extractDecl(n))` fix at web-extract.mjs:114 is real: point-free would have passed map's index as `src`.

findings.claim: The new whole-body pin covers exactly three functions, but the iOS behaviour it is protecting is computed by their collaborators, which remain substring-pinned and therefore insertion-blind. Splicing `if 1 == 1 { return true }` into endsFirstOK (Daily.swift:128) makes the ends-first objective un-violatable — the iOS tier chip never goes ✗ and auto-play spends a live ends-first tier, bug/WF-4 shipped back — and zeroing liveAttempt's moves (Game.swift:967) makes the iOS moves-family look-ahead never refuse. Both leave the whole suite green.
findings.note: MUTATION-PROVEN this round with my own manifest (0 errors, so the survivals are real applies): y-ios-endsFirstOK-early-true SURVIVED, y-ios-liveAttempt-zero-moves SURVIVED. Cheapest containment without a Swift unit-test target: extend IOS_BODIES to the seven checker helpers plus liveAttempt (they are short and stable) — or accept it explicitly and record which iOS code is text-pinned only. Do NOT chase this with more substring pins; substrings are exactly what both mutants walked through.

findings.claim: stripSwiftComments ended a /* block at the FIRST */, but Swift block comments nest, so a nested comment inside a pinned body leaked the outer comment's tail (braces included) into the brace matcher and a pure comment edit failed the pin with 'a statement was added'.
findings.note: VERIFIED. The depth counter at :180-185 matches Swift's lexer (nesting tracked on /* and */ only, strings not special inside a comment — same as Swift). Self-test at :233-239 covers nesting, // with a brace, and a comment marker inside a string literal; mutant c-pin-stripper-not-nesting-aware killed (5/5, 0 errors, manifest re-run by me). I also checked the new fail-loud guard at :224 is actually reachable: for both `"""` and `#"` the opening delimiter necessarily precedes any `}` inside the literal, so a body truncated by a mis-scanned literal still contains the delimiter and the assertion fires rather than pinning garbage.

findings.claim: The calendar-cell locator these tripwires depend on has never matched anything: calCell applies .accessibilityLabel("Aug 30") to a bare ZStack that is not an accessibility element (no .accessibilityElement(children:.combine), no button trait), so XCUITest sees only the child staticText "30". Round 3 replaced the XCTSkipUnless that was hiding this with a hard XCTAssertFalse, so the class is now RED on the shipping tree: testPlayButtonNamesTheSelectedDay fails at RegressionDailyCalendarTests.swift:135 with 'no calendar cell for Aug 30'. testTappingALockedFutureDayExplainsWhy uses the identical query shape and only escaped because 2026-08-31 is the last day of the month (date-keyed skip); it goes red on 2026-09-01. The same missing accessibility element is a shipping VoiceOver defect: every calendar cell announces as the bare number, with no month, no earned tiers, no lock state, and no button trait.
findings.note: VERIFIED BY RUNNING on udid 5329250C (xcodebuild test-without-building -scheme Causeway -parallel-testing-enabled NO -only-testing:CausewayUITests/RegressionDailyCalendarTests): 3 tests, 1 skipped, 1 FAILURE. testCalendarLegendNamesTheSameDayPip passed; testPlayButtonNamesTheSelectedDay FAILED at :135; testTappingALockedFutureDayExplainsWhy skipped via the new last-day-of-month guard. The implementer only ran `build-for-testing`, and verify_cmd is node-only, so nothing in the loop executes this target — the red shipped unseen. The APP behaviour is fine: I drove the simulator by hand (Daily -> scroll -> tap the Aug 30 cell) and the button correctly reads 'Play Aug 30'. So this is a test/accessibility defect, not a product regression. FIX: add `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` (or .ignore) next to the existing .accessibilityLabel at DailyView.swift:626, and give the cell `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)` + `.accessibilityIdentifier("daily.cal.<idx>")` as the round-2 fragment already proposed; then re-run BOTH calendar tests, not just build-for-testing.

findings.claim: Three re-deal entry points never consult hasLiveGame, so they still destroy a live game — and a live ⏰ grace — with no dialog, defeating the closeout's parity claim. On the web, the Daily sheet's Play/Replay button calls playChallenge(day) straight from its onclick (index.html:1587-1588) and 'Show me how to win' guards on its own weaker `challengeDay!=null && moveCount>0` (index.html:1522); the iOS twins of both DO route through hasLiveGame (DailyView.swift:313, :375). On BOTH platforms the Wins sheet deals a seed with no gate at all (WinsView.swift:87 playEntered, WinsView.swift:108 the solved-deal row; web winsPlay at index.html:1826). A player mid-attempt on yesterday's challenge who opens Wins and taps a past deal loses that day's ⏰ Same-day forever with no warning. The comment at index.html:1863 asserting 'the Daily sheet has guarded exactly this destruction since round 0' is false for playChallenge.
findings.note: Pre-existing, surfaced by auditing this closeout's shipping predicate. Confirmed by reading every caller of playChallenge/showSolution/deal on both platforms (grep of `game.deal(`/`game.playChallenge(`/`game.showSolution(` under ios/Causeway/Causeway/Views and of `confirmReset()`/`playChallenge(` in index.html). ContentView.swift:913-914 is the WIN overlay, where hasLiveGame is false by construction — not part of this. FIX SHAPE: route web playChallenge's two onclick buttons and showSolution through confirmReset()/hasLiveGame(), and gate WinsView.playEntered + the solved-deal row on game.hasLiveGame the same way ContentView.requestReset does.

findings.claim: testPlayButtonNamesTheSelectedDay guards only the pool's START (yesterday >= 2026-08-01) and not its END. daily-pool.json seeds 61 days, i.e. 2026-08-01..2026-09-30, so from 2026-10-02 the yesterday cell is unavailable: tapping it sets lockedDay instead of selecting the day, play.label never names it, and the test hard-fails with a message that blames the calendar grid. Separately, round 3 widened the locked-note assertion to `contains("unlocks on the day itself") || contains("No challenge on")`, so after 2026-09-30 testTappingALockedFutureDayExplainsWhy passes through the out-of-pool branch and no longer exercises the locked-seeded-day path (ux/WF-13) it was written for.
findings.note: Pool size read from ios/Causeway/Causeway/daily-pool.json: epoch 2026-08-01, 61 days. Survives fixing the locator, so file it separately.
